key_insight: In laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel, higher laser power and current strengthen molten-pool convection and widen/deepen the weld, while higher travel speed lowers heat input and shrinks the weld.
engineering_relevance: These process-window trends help optimize joint quality and arc stability for low-expansion Invar steel used in precision aerospace tooling and molds.
method: Numerical simulation of molten-pool flow and heat transfer
High-speed photography of arc and pool behavior
Parametric study of laser power, welding speed, and welding current
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coupled simulation and high-speed imaging results across laser power (5–6 kW), welding speed (0.5–0.8 m/min), and current (150–170 A) to link process settings with penetration, weld width, pool flow, and arc deflection/stability.
watch_item: The reported trends are process-window specific, so transferability to other joint geometries, shielding conditions, or thicknesses should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Molten pool dynamic behavior and arc characteristics in laser-TIG hybrid welding of Invar steel
